summary.text: Douglas Ollivant, a Republican retired Army lieutenant colonel who served combat tours in Iraq and leads a consulting firm, lost the November 3, 2026 election for Virginia's 7th District to Rep. Eugene Vindman.
He later directed Iraq policy at the National Security Council.

paragraphs.text: Ollivant lives in Culpeper County and previously lived in Falls Church; his campaign describes him as a husband, father of seven and grandfather of two.
Ballotpedia lists a bachelor's degree, a master's degree and a doctorate from Wheaton College, James Madison University and Indiana University.
Ollivant served in the U.S. Army and reached the rank of lieutenant colonel; news reports describe two combat tours in Iraq and service as an adviser to coalition forces in Afghanistan.
He taught at the U.S. Military Academy at West Point, and he served as Director for Iraq at the National Security Council under Presidents George W. Bush and Barack Obama.
Ollivant is managing partner of Mantid International, LLC, a compliance and business-intelligence consulting firm that, per a news report, has offices in Washington, D.C., Guam, Beirut and Baghdad.
He won the Republican nomination in the August 4, 2026 primary, defeating Philip Harding and Rick Smithers.
His campaign emphasized energy costs, housing supply, spending cuts and national security.
He received 37.6% of the vote to Eugene Vindman's 59.8%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
